ms.report:
Demo Day Results:
The following document provides the outcomes of our Demo Day, including an anonymised list of attendees and the scoring of each participating project based on their performance. Starting the second page of the document, you can see on the very right the company and title of the attendee. We also added a screenshot of our Luma invite page, which demonstrates that we invited over 350 investors and beyond for the Demo Day:
Demo Day Outcomes & Scoring
Screenshot of invited individuals
Project Materials:
This document contains all data rooms and pitch decks submitted by participating projects. While most materials are publicly accessible, some require a request for access:
Project Data Rooms & Pitch Decks (All Data Rooms are now Public)
Here you can find learning materials and templates for the data room, which we provided to the startups in a 60-minute workshop for their projects.
Demo Day Recording:
A full recording of the Demo Day is available here:
Demo Day Video
To address the question about fundraising targets: early-stage funding rounds are highly individual for each team. The amount to be raised depends on the capital needs, while the target valuation is strongly influenced by factors such as industry, product, and traction. For reference, you can find common pre-seed and seed examples here.
During the planning phase, we initially considered appointing four judges to conduct a structured 5-minute Q&A session following each project pitch. However, in alignment with recent best practices and observable trends toward more concise and engaging Demo Day formats, we deliberately optimized the event structure.
By removing the formal judge panel and post-pitch Q&A sessions, the overall event duration was reduced by approximately 30–45 minutes. This adjustment ensured that all participating startups, particularly those pitching toward the end of the agenda, benefited from consistently high audience attendance and attention.
